title: Category budget and monthly spending report
instructions:
Implement `BudgetTracker` in `budget.py`. All money is integer cents; date, month, IDs, and
categories are strings. Expenses have positive amounts; refunds have negative amounts.
- `BudgetTracker()` starts with no entries and no limits.
- `add(entry_id: str, date: str, category: str, amount: int) -> None` stores an entry.
  The ID must be nonempty and not already stored. Date must be exactly `YYYY-MM-DD` with ASCII
  digits and a valid calendar date (years 0001–9999). Strip surrounding whitespace from category;
  the result must be nonempty and remains case-sensitive. Amount must be nonzero.
  Invalid input raises `ValueError` and leaves state unchanged.
- `remove(entry_id: str) -> bool` removes an entry, returning True if found and False otherwise.
  Removed IDs may be reused.
- `set_limit(category: str, cents: int) -> None` strips/validates category as above and sets its
  monthly limit. Negative cents raises `ValueError` without changing state; zero is allowed.
  Limits apply to every month and setting again replaces the old limit.
- `report(month: str) -> dict` accepts exactly `YYYY-MM` with ASCII digits, years 0001–9999,
  and months 01–12; otherwise raise `ValueError`. Return:
  `{"month": month, "total": int, "categories": list[dict]}`.
  Include each category with an entry in that month (even if its net amount is zero), plus each
  category with a limit. Sort categories lexicographically. Each row has exactly
  `{"category": str, "spent": int, "limit": int|None, "remaining": int|None}`.
  Spent and total sum signed entry amounts in that month. Missing limits give None for both
  limit and remaining; otherwise remaining = limit - spent, possibly negative.
Reports are fresh independent containers; callers may mutate them without affecting the tracker.
No persistence or floating-point currency conversion is required. Internal helpers may be changed.

## Files
- `budget.py`
